fixes.note: pack_test.c has a new PT7 block after PT6. It runs under the 64 MiB cap (lj52_mem_settotal is re-asserted) and makes its calls through a new helper, packst(), which uses lua_pcall the way PT4 calls pack. PT7a: pack('c2147483392','') gives LUA_ERRRUN with the exact text 'not enough memory for buffer allocation'. PT7b: pack('c2147483391c1','','') gives the same. PT7c: pack('c2147483391','') gives LUA_ERRMEM with the exact text 'not enough memory'. PT7d: pack('c2000000000c2000000000','',{}) gives LUA_ERRRUN, a message starting 'bad argument #3 ' and containing '(string expected, got table)'. The measured text is "bad argument #3 to '?' (string expected, got table)". Note: c2147483392 is itself a total of 0x7fffff00 == LJ_MAX_STR (lj_def.h:49,54), so PT7a is a boundary case too, not only PT7b. I checked by reading that nothing large is allocated. In PT7a and PT7b, D4 (oclj_strpack.c:624-625) raises before lua_newuserdata (:629). In PT7d, pass 1 raises at arg 3 before D4. In PT7c, lua_newuserdata (lj_api.c:752, size <= LJ_MAX_UDATA) reaches lj_mem_newgco, which calls lj52_alloc. In C mode lj52_alloc returns NULL at lj52shim.c:431-438 because delta > total - used + credit + lend. The credit is at most G (512 KiB) + KSLICE (16 KiB) (:1482-1483, :1576-1588), and the lend is at most 4 KiB past the top (:1620). That return comes before lj52_back (:440), the only call that reaches the system allocator. lj_mem_newgco then raises lj_err_mem (lj_gc.c:885-889). Measured: used is 0.05 MiB after PT7c.
